rv.q: Ultimately, Pot Girls crackles with ensemble energy and sharp ideas, offering an engaging, thought‑rich night of theatre for anyone drawn to fresh feminist work.
Bakari's dazzling direction and the stellar cast make this simply one of the best shows I've seen so far this year (granted, the year is young, but still).
Paul Michael Thomson’s new play is really clever and often both funny and thought-provoking.
Better to be over-ambitious than play it safe.

For those that are looking for a well-written, spectacularly acted, and social commentary play that balances comedy, tragedy, and questioning our daily lives, Pot Girls would be an excellent choice for you!
Thompson's script and director Ayanna Bria Bakari collaborate seamlessly to create a thought-provoking and deeply human play.
While I enjoyed the play, I am not sure it is for everyone. It does deal with sexual situations, drugs, racism, and has a few spots that seemed disjointed to me.

cn.t: Critics praise this sharp, funny feminist play as a worthy homage to Caryl Churchill's "Top Girls," with a superb cast bringing vivid theatricality and thought-provoking commentary on art, activism, and women's history across time periods.
